verdicts.evidence: Code read at chunk-INI453VG.js:57 (stepDays = 0.02) and :64 (applying = |nextSeparation - angle| < orb) matches the citation. Analytically, with the linear model the stepped orb is |0.02*rel - orb|, which is < orb iff orb > 0.01*rel, so every applying aspect with orb < 0.01*|relSpeed| is reported separating; numerically the boundary sits exactly there (rel 6.1: orb 0.0611 -> true, 0.0609 -> false; rel 12.22: 0.1221 -> false). Shipped dist findAspects on Moon 99.9 (13.2 deg/d) vs Sun 100.0 (0.98) returns {conjunction, orb 0.10, applying:false} although exactness is 11 min away; Moon 0.13 before trine -> true; retrograde Mercury case -> true (correct). Independent 2024 scan (every 30 min, computeBodies, reference = real motion: orb at t vs orb at t+60 s from recomputed longitudes, NOT the auditor's linear model): 236,910 aspects, 486 misclassified (0.205%; auditor 510 with the linear reference, the 24-case difference is boundary cases where the two references differ), zero separating-reported-applying, all 486 with orb <= 0.01*relSpeed, max misclassified orb 0.1484 deg. One aside in the auditor's evidence is inexact: 83 of the 486 are non-Moon pairs (Sun-Uranus 5, Venus-Saturn 6, Mars-Saturn 3, ...), so the window applies to every pair, merely most often to the Moon. Severity blocking is earned under the rules: a shipped boolean is deterministically wrong in a reproducible window, and STRATEGY.md advertises applying/separating as a feature.

Additional observation from the finding-3 ladder: with the polar constant relaxed, the same mean-obliquity pairing produces cusp errors up to 8081 arcsec (2.2 deg) at |lat| 66.5, so this fix is a prerequisite for widening the Placidus band. Severity major is earned (accuracy gap materially below Swiss, 0.14 deg exceeding the project's own 0.1 deg ASC gate at lat 66); the README overstatement is separately finding 12.

Phenomenon and numbers confirmed. chunk-H7RJKCBO.js:46 is the hard constant (|lat| > 66 -> null) and :91-107 substitutes whole-sign cusps with fellBack=true. Rovaniemi 1995-06-15T12:00Z 66.5034N 25.7294E: shipped computeChart -> houses.system 'whole', flags ['polar-fallback'], cusps 180,210,240; Swiss houses_ex 'P' (SWIEPH) succeeds with cusp11 147.0393, cusp12 172.8253, ASC/MC agreeing with the engine to 1.5 arcsec. Swiss ladder (8 hours x lat 66.0..67.0, four epochs): Placidus fails first at 66.55 in 1800 (90 - eps_true = 66.5326), at 66.57 in 1995 and 2000 (limit 66.5625/66.5620), at 66.6 in 2200 (66.5892) - i.e. exactly |lat| >= 90 - eps_true, confirming the auditor's dynamic limit. Copying the dist chunk to scratch with the constant replaced by |lat| >= 90 - input.obliquity and running the 336-case 66.05-66.55 ladder (both hemispheres, 1800/2000/2200, 8 hours): status agrees with Swiss in 336/336 (16 nulls = the 16 Swiss failures), and with Swiss ARMC + true obliquity the engine's iteration matches Swiss cusps to 0.0085 arcsec, so convergence is not the obstacle; the shipped code refuses all 320 cases Swiss computes; whole-sign fallback vs Swiss Placidus differs by up to 147.5 deg. Two corrections: (a) pyswisseph 2.10.03 raises only 'swisseph.houses_ex: error' - the 'within polar circle, switched to Porphyry' text is the C library's serr and is not surfaced by the wrapper; (b) severity. The behaviour is documented (STRATEGY.md 'hard fallback to Whole Sign above 66 deg', README section 2), flagged in the result, leaves ASC/MC correct, and affects a band of at most 0.53-0.59 deg of latitude, so it is a small real defect rather than a gap that keeps the stack materially below Swiss.
verdicts.correctedClaim: placidusCusps refuses at a hard |lat| > 66 while Swiss computes Placidus up to |lat| < 90 - eps_true (66.53 in 1800, 66.56 today, 66.59 in 2200); in the 66.0-66.56 band the engine returns a flagged whole-sign fallback although its own iteration converges there and matches Swiss cusps to 0.0085 arcsec given Swiss inputs. The fallback is documented and flagged and ASC/MC stay correct, so this is a narrow, documented conservative limit; note that widening it without first fixing finding 1 would expose 2.2 deg cusp errors at 66.5.

notes: All scripts and outputs are under <audit>/verify/angles-houses-aspects/ (swiss_probe.py/.out, swiss_grid.py -> swiss_grid.json, engine_grid.mjs -> engine_gridA_report.json + engine_gridA_rows.json, applying_scan.mjs -> applying_scan.json/.out, houses_relaxed.mjs + ladder.mjs -> ladder.out, erfa_spot.py + spot_swiss.json). The worktree was only read; the relaxed-limit test used a copy of the dist chunk in scratch. Every Swiss call was checked for the SWIEPH flag (calc_ut retflag 258; 0 non-SWIEPH cases in the grid dump). No Horizons requests were made (Horizons computes no houses); the independent arbiter for finding 1's supporting claims was pyerfa 2.0.1.5 from the phase-1 auditor's venv (which lacks swisseph, so Swiss and ERFA halves were run in separate venvs and joined through JSON). Overall: findings 1, 2 and 7 reproduce within their stated numbers and their severities are earned; finding 3 reproduces exactly but is a documented, flagged, 0.56-degree conservative limit and is downgraded to minor. Two evidence-level inaccuracies in the report, neither changing a verdict: finding 2's 'all involving the Moon' (83 of 486 misclassifications are non-Moon pairs under a real-motion reference) and finding 3's quoted pyswisseph error text (the wrapper raises 'swisseph.houses_ex: error'). One cross-finding dependency worth carrying into the report: relaxing the Placidus limit (finding 3) before fixing the obliquity pairing (finding 1) would expose 2.2-degree cusp errors at 66.5 degrees.
